title: Oncall & Incident Response Playbook Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Communications
author: Maya Patel
summary: Comprehensive playbook for Redwood Inference on-call and incident response: defines incident lifecycle, severity definitions, runbook templates, on-call rotations and escalation, game day practices, postmortem process, and customer/status communications templates.
body:
Purpose

This playbook describes the standard process and supporting artifacts for handling production incidents at Redwood Inference. It is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, support staff, product owners, and incident reviewers. Follow this document for consistent detection, mitigation, communication, and learning.

Scope

- Applies to all customer-facing services (API gateways, inference runtime, routing, billing, console, and telemetry pipelines).
- Includes hosted, dedicated, and private control-plane incidents when our control plane or management interfaces are involved.

Key goals

1. Restore service quickly and safely.
2. Communicate clearly to internal stakeholders and customers.
3. Preserve evidence for post-incident analysis.
4. Reduce recurrence via actionable follow-ups.

Roles & responsibilities

- Primary on-call (Pager): First responder responsible for triage, initial mitigation, and running the runbook.
- Secondary on-call (Escalation): Assists when primary is overloaded or escalation criteria met.
- Incident Commander (IC): Takes ownership for coordination on Sev2+/major incidents. IC is not necessarily the primary engineer.
- Communications lead: Owns status page updates, internal Slack incident channel, and customer comms drafts.
- SRE lead: Ensures postmortem, follow-ups, and SLA reconciliation.
- Product owner: Validates customer impact and priority for rollouts/feature flags.

Contact channels and tooling

- Paging: PagerDuty (service: redwood-production) \u2014 use severity-based escalation policies.
- Incident channel: #inc-<service>-YYYYMMDD on Slack (auto-created by PagerDuty integration).
- Status page: status.redwood.ai for public updates; internal draft on /confluence/status-drafts.
- Incident tracking: JIRA project INCD (issue type: Incident).
- Postmortem: Confluence template (use this page), link from JIRA incident ticket.
- Artifact collection: Service logs (ELK), traces (Tempo), metrics (Prometheus/Grafana), and runtime snapshots (SRE snapshot store).

Severity definitions (with SLO tie-in)

- Sev 1 (P0) \u2014 Major outage: System-wide customer impact, >50% requests failing or >3x latency SLO violation for >10 minutes, significant revenue loss risk. Pager escalation immediate; declare incident within 5 minutes.
- Sev 2 (P1) \u2014 Partial outage or major degradation: Important subset of customers or endpoints impacted, >10% error rate sustained for >15 minutes or persistent degraded throughput.
- Sev 3 (P2) \u2014 Localized issue: Single tenant, single region, or non-critical backend degraded with workaround available.
- Sev 4 (P3) \u2014 Non-urgent operational issue: Metrics anomaly, minor bug, or request for follow-up work.

Incident lifecycle (high level)

1. Detect: Alert or customer report. Triage immediately.
2. Triage: Confirm impact, assign severity, create JIRA INCD ticket, and open Slack incident channel.
3. Mitigate: Apply safe mitigation steps from relevant runbook. If mitigation is unclear, escalate to secondary.
4. Stabilize: Confirm traffic/requests return to acceptable levels and monitor for recurrence.
5. Communicate: Update internal stakeholders and public status page where applicable.
6. Post-incident: Write postmortem, create action items with owners and target dates, and schedule follow-up review.

Runbook template (use as checklist for all Sev1/Sev2)

- Title: <service> \u2014 <symptom> runbook
- Purpose: Short description of symptom and impact.
- When to use: Trigger conditions, alert names, thresholds.
- Pager steps (first 10 minutes):
  1. Acknowledge pager in PagerDuty.
  2. Create JIRA INCD ticket with initial notes and severity.
  3. Open Slack incident channel and post initial summary: who, what, when, impact, and next steps.
  4. Run quick health checks (endpoint pings, API check, key metric dashboards).
- Quick mitigation (ordered):
  1. Apply circuit-breaker: disable non-essential routes via router config (cli: rwctl route disable <route>).
  2. Scale inference workers in the affected pool: terraform apply -var=pool=<name> -target=module.pool_scale (or use console: Dedicated -> Pools -> Scale).
  3. Roll back recent deployment: kubectl -n <ns> rollout undo deployment/<service> --to-revision=<rev>.
  4. Re-route traffic to failover region: rwctl routing promote --from <region> --to <failover-region>.
- Evidence collection (immediate):
  - Save relevant logs (ELK query) to incident artifact storage.
  - Snapshot Prometheus graphs for error rate, p95 latency, and throughput.
  - Save an example failing request ID and full trace URL.
- Escalation path: If unresolved after 20 minutes or if customer-impact grows, notify on-call secondary, then SRE lead, then Eng Director.
- Post-mitigation checks: Verify key SLOs (error rate < 1% for the impacted endpoints, p95 latency within 1.5x baseline) for 30 minutes before declaring resolved.

Example quick-check CLI snippets

- Check API health: curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://api.redwood.ai/health
- List current inference pool utilization: rwctl pool status --name inference-pool-prod
- Fetch latest errors: curl -s "https://elk.redwood.ai/query?q=service:inference AND level:ERROR&from=-15m"

Escalation & rotation policy

- Primary on-call: 8-hour shifts, weekdays covered 24/7 by rotating team. Weekend shifts are 12 hours.
- Rotation schedule: Rotations are maintained in PagerDuty with owners set 6 weeks in advance.
- Escalation timeline: Acknowledge immediate; escalate to secondary after 5 minutes if not acknowledged; escalate to IC after 20 minutes of unresolved Sev1/Sev2.
- Out-of-hours: Oncall may call in an engineer from the owning service team if runbook requires domain expertise.

On-call conduct and best practices

- Always update the incident channel on each major step. Small updates are fine (\"triage started\", \"mitigation applied\").
- Prefer safe, reversible mitigations first (traffic routing, scaling, feature flags) before rolling back code.
- Preserve logs and traces before doing destructive actions.

Game days (practical exercises)

- Frequency: Quarterly company-level game day + monthly service-level tabletop for high-impact services.
- Goals: Validate runbooks, exercise communication templates, measure time-to-detect and time-to-resolve, and stress test failover policies.
- Example exercises:
  - Simulated regional outage (failover routing exercise).
  - Cache layer corruption (test fallback to cold KV).
  - Degraded model weights (simulate inference runtime OOM and test quantized fallback).
- Metrics to collect during game day: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to mitigate (MTTM), mean time to recover (MTTR), and number of incomplete runbook steps.

Postmortems and blameless review process

- Required for: All Sev1 incidents and Sev2 incidents with customer impact or SLA violations.
- Template (use JIRA link to confluence template):
  - Summary: Short one-line incident summary.
  - Timeline: Chronological events with timestamps and links to traces/logs.
  - Impact: Customers, regions, revenue, SLA breaches.
  - Root cause analysis: What directly caused the incident and why preventative controls failed.
  - Mitigations: Short-term mitigations applied.
  - Corrective actions: Specific action items, owner, target date, and risk level.
  - Postmortem review notes and retrospective findings.
- Review cadence: Postmortem draft due within 72 hours; 1-week review meeting with SRE, owners, and product; action items tracked to completion in JIRA.

Customer & status page communications templates

- Status page template (public):
  - Title: [Major Outage] <service> experiencing elevated error rates
  - Impact: Short summary of affected customers and endpoints.
  - Current status: Detecting / Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Restored
  - Next update: ETA for next update or \"TBD\"
  - Details: What we are doing and recommended customer workarounds.

- Customer email template (to affected customers for Sev1/Sev2):
  Subject: Incident impacting Redwood <service> \u2014 <date/time>
  Hi <Customer Name>,

  We experienced a disruption to <service> between <start> and <end>. During the incident you may have seen <symptoms>. We have applied mitigation steps and services are restored for most customers. We will follow up with a detailed postmortem and next steps.

  If you continue to experience issues, please reply to this message or open a support ticket (link).

  Sincerely,
  Redwood Inference Ops Team

- Internal Slack incident message template:
  @channel
  INCIDENT: <service> \u2014 <symptom>
  Severity: <sev>
  Impact: <customers/regions>
  IC: <name> | Primary: <name> | Communications: <name>
  Actions: <short list of actions taken>

Operational metrics and dashboards to monitor

- Per-service dashboard: error rate, p50/p95 latency, throughput, success rate by model variant, queue length, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.
- SLO dashboard: % requests meeting latency and error SLO by region and by customer tier.
- Paging thresholds: error-rate > 10% for 5m (Sev2), error-rate > 50% for 3m (Sev1), sustained p95 > 3x baseline for 10m (Sev1).

Retention and evidence policy

- Attach all incident artifacts to the JIRA INCD ticket within 48 hours.
- Retain logs/traces for 90 days for incidents; extended retention for regulatory customers as per contract.

Change control during incidents

- Production changes that are not emergency mitigations must be frozen until incident declared resolved.
- Emergency deploys must be logged and communicated in the incident channel with rollforward/rollback plans.

Continuous improvement and follow-up

- Action items from postmortems are tracked in JIRA and linked to the original incident.
- SRE quarterly reliability review consolidates action completion rates, recurring failure modes, and game-day performance.
- Maintain runbooks as living documents: update after each incident or game day within 7 days.

Appendix: Quick links and runbook index

- Runbooks (examples):
  - inference-runtime-high-error-rate
  - api-gateway-timeouts
  - routing-failover-region
  - billing-tenant-quotas-issue

- Templates and forms: Postmortem template (Confluence), Incident JIRA template (INCD), Status page draft doc.

Ownership and review

- Document owner: SRE team (sre@redwood.ai).
- Review cadence: Annual review or after any Sev1 incident.

If you are on-call now and need a refresher: follow the Runbook Template checklist above, acknowledge your pager, and post initial message in the incident channel. For questions about rotations or policies, contact the SRE lead or the on-call schedule owner.
